items.title: Two Kinds of Consumption: Desire's Objects, and the Dharma

items.zh: 又外有欲者，受用欲塵。聖慧命者，受用正法。由五種相故有差別。由此因緣，說聖慧命者以無上慧命清淨自活。
items.en: Further, one whose desire is directed outward consumes the objects of desire; one whose life is sustained by noble wisdom consumes the true Dharma. These differ by five distinguishing marks; for this reason, it is said that one whose life is sustained by noble wisdom lives on this unsurpassed, pure wisdom-life.

items.zh: 何等為五？一、受用正法者，不染污故；二、受用正法者，極畢竟故；三、受用正法者，一向定故；四、受用正法者，與餘慧命者不共故；五、受用正法者，有真實樂故，摧伏魔怨故。
items.en: What are the five? First, consuming the true Dharma is undefiled; second, it is utterly final; third, it is one-pointedly certain; fourth, it is not shared with other so-called wisdom-lives; fifth, it carries genuine pleasure, and overcomes the enemy that is Māra.

items.zh: 此中諸受欲者所有欲樂是隨順喜處，貪愛所隨故；是隨順憂處，瞋恚所隨故；是隨順捨處，無簡擇捨之所隨故。聖慧命者受用正法則不如是。
items.en: Here, the pleasure of desire experienced by those who consume desire's objects is, when it leans towards joy, followed by craving; when it leans towards sorrow, followed by hatred; and when it leans towards equanimity, followed by an equanimity devoid of any real discernment. One whose life is sustained by noble wisdom, consuming the true Dharma, is not like this.

items.zh: 又諸有欲者受用欲塵，從不可知本際以來，以無常故，捨餘欲塵得餘欲塵；或於一時都無所得。聖慧命者受用正法則不如是。
items.en: Further, those who consume the objects of desire, since beginningless time, forever impermanent, abandon one object of desire only to seize another — or, at times, gain nothing at all. One whose life is sustained by noble wisdom, consuming the true Dharma, is not like this.

items.title: Unwavering, and Uncommon With Other Paths

items.zh: 又受欲者受用欲時，即於此事一起喜愛，一起憂恚；復即於彼或時生喜，或時生憂。聖慧命者受用正法則不如是。
items.en: Further, when one who consumes desire's objects consumes them, joy and delight arise together over this very matter, and sorrow and resentment arise together as well; and towards that same object, joy arises at one time and sorrow at another. One whose life is sustained by noble wisdom, consuming the true Dharma, is not like this.

items.zh: 又諸離欲外慧命者，於種種見趣、自分別所起邪勝解處，其心猛利，種種取著，恒為欲染之所隨逐；雖已離欲，復還退起。聖慧命者受用正法則不如是。
items.en: Further, non-Buddhist practitioners who claim wisdom yet have merely become free of desire, caught up in various views and in the distorted convictions their own conceptual thinking has generated, hold to these with a fierce and manifold attachment, and remain forever pursued by the very taint of desire — though already free of desire, they fall back into it once again. One whose life is sustained by noble wisdom, consuming the true Dharma, is not like this.

items.title: Genuine Joy That Conquers the Four Māras

items.zh: 又受欲者及諸世間已離欲者，所有欲樂及離欲樂，皆非真實，皆為魔怨之所隨逐；如幻、如響、如影、如焰、如夢所見、猶如幻作諸莊嚴具。
items.en: Further, the pleasure of desire enjoyed by those who consume desire's objects, and the pleasure of freedom from desire enjoyed by those in the world already free of it, are both alike unreal, and both alike remain pursued by the enemy that is Māra — like an illusion, like an echo, like a shadow, like a mirage, like what is seen in a dream, like ornaments conjured by a magician.

items.zh: 又著樂愚夫諸受欲者，及諸世間已離欲者，凡所受用，猶如癲狂、如醉亂等；未制魔軍而有受用。是故彼樂為非真實，亦不能制所有魔事。聖慧命者受用正法則不如是。
items.en: Further, the foolish, pleasure-attached consumers of desire, and those in the world already free of desire, both consume it as though deranged, as though drunk and disordered — enjoying it without ever having subdued Māra's own army. For this reason, that pleasure is unreal, and cannot overcome any of Māra's works. One whose life is sustained by noble wisdom, consuming the true Dharma, is not like this.

items.title: Observing the Body as a Boil, and the Three Feelings as Its Symptoms

items.zh: 復次，三界有情所依之身，當云何觀？謂如毒熱癰、麁重所隨故。
items.en: Further, how should the body that beings of the three realms depend on be observed? As a poisonous, feverish boil, followed everywhere by its own underlying affliction.

items.zh: 即於此身樂受生時，當云何觀？謂如毒熱癰暫遇冷觸。即於此身苦受生時，當云何觀？謂如毒熱癰為熱灰所觸。
items.en: When a pleasant feeling arises within this very body, how should it be observed? As when a poisonous, feverish boil is briefly touched by something cool. When a painful feeling arises within this very body, how should it be observed? As when a poisonous, feverish boil is touched by hot ash.

items.zh: 即於此身不苦不樂受生時，當云何觀？謂如毒熱癰離冷熱等觸，自性毒熱而本住故。
items.en: When a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises within this very body, how should it be observed? As when a poisonous, feverish boil, touched by neither cold nor heat, simply rests in its own underlying feverish, poisoned nature.

items.title: Three Kinds of Suffering Hidden in the Three Feelings

items.zh: 薄伽梵說：當知樂受，壞苦故苦；苦受，苦苦故苦；不苦不樂受，行苦故苦。又
items.en: The Blessed One said: it should be understood that pleasant feeling is suffering through the suffering of change; painful feeling is suffering through the suffering of pain itself; and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is suffering through the suffering inherent in all conditioned formations.

items.title: Three Kinds of Joy, and the Deepest Bliss of All

items.zh: 說有有愛味喜、有離愛味喜、有勝離愛味喜。如是等類，如經廣說。應知墮二界攝。
items.en: It is further said that there is joy with a savour of craving, joy free of that savour, and a superior joy still more free of it. These should be understood as comprised within two realms.

items.zh: 又薄伽梵建立想受滅樂為樂中第一。此依住樂，非謂受樂。
items.en: Further, the Blessed One established the bliss of the cessation of ideation and feeling as foremost among all forms of bliss. This is the bliss of abiding, not the bliss of feeling.

items.zh: 又說有三種樂。謂離貪、離瞋、離癡。此三種樂唯無漏界中可得，是故此樂名為常樂，無漏界攝。
items.en: It is further said that there are three kinds of bliss: freedom from the craving of desire, freedom from the craving of hatred, and freedom from the craving of delusion. These three kinds of bliss can be found only within the uncontaminated realm; for this reason, this bliss is called constant bliss, comprised within the uncontaminated realm.

items.title: Four Kinds of Food That Sustain the Three Realms

items.zh: 復次，飲食受用者，謂三界將生、已生、有情壽命安住。
items.en: Further, as for the consumption of food: it is what sustains the lifespan of beings across the three realms, whether about to be born or already born.

items.zh: 此中當知觸、意思、識、三種食故，一切三界有情壽命安住。段食一種，唯令欲界有情壽命安住。又
items.en: Here it should be understood that it is by reason of three kinds of food — contact, mental intention, and consciousness — that all beings throughout the three realms have their lifespan sustained. The one remaining kind, edible food, sustains only the lifespan of beings within the desire realm.

items.zh: 於那落迦受生有情，有微細段食。謂腑藏中有微動風，由此因緣，彼得久住。
items.en: Further, beings reborn in the hells have a subtle kind of edible food: a faintly stirring wind within their internal organs, by reason of which they continue to endure.

items.zh: 餓鬼、傍生、人中，有麁段食。謂作分段而噉食之。
items.en: Among hungry ghosts, animals, and humans, there is coarse edible food: food taken in discrete portions and actually eaten.

items.zh: 復有微細食。謂住羯羅藍等位有情，及欲界諸天。由彼食已，所有段食流入一切身分支節，尋即消化，無有便穢。
items.en: There is, further, a subtle food: that of beings dwelling at the kalala and similar early embryonic stages, and of the desire realm's gods. Once such a being has eaten, this edible food flows into every limb and joint of the body and is immediately dissolved, leaving no waste behind.

items.zh: 復次，婬欲受用者，諸那落迦中所有有情皆無婬事。所以者何？由彼有情長時無間多受種種極猛利苦。由此因緣，彼諸有情，若男於女不起女欲，若女於男不起男欲，何況展轉二二交會。
items.en: Further, as for the consumption of sexual activity: beings throughout every hell engage in no such act at all. Why is this? Because those beings, for a long, unbroken span of time, undergo suffering of every kind, extremely intense throughout. Because of this, among them, no man ever conceives desire towards a woman, nor any woman towards a man — much less do the two sexual organs ever actually come together.

items.zh: 若鬼、傍生、人中，所有依身苦樂相雜，故有婬欲。男女展轉二二交會，不淨流出。欲界諸天雖行婬欲，無此不淨；然於根門有風氣出，煩惱便息。
items.en: Among hungry ghosts, animals, and humans, the body they depend on mixes pain and pleasure together, and so sexual desire is present: male and female come together, and impure fluid is released. The desire realm's gods, though they too engage in sexual activity, produce no such impurity; rather, a breath of air simply passes through the sexual organ, and the affliction is thereby put to rest.

items.zh: 四大王眾天，二二交會，熱惱方息。如四大王眾天，三十三天亦爾。時分天唯互相抱，熱惱便息。知足天、唯相執手，熱惱便息。樂化天相顧而笑，熱惱便息。他化自在天眼相顧視，熱惱便息。
items.en: Among the Four Great Kings, it is the actual union of the two organs that lays the affliction to rest. As with the Four Great Kings, so too with the Thirty-Three. The Time-Divisions Heaven's beings need only embrace one another for the affliction to be put to rest. The Contentment Heaven's beings need only hold hands. The Heaven of Delighting in Transformation's beings need only exchange a smiling glance. The Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations' beings need only look at one another with their eyes.

blocks.text: Today's reading contains one of the most quoted passages in the treatise: the body as a poisonous boil, and the three feelings as three kinds of suffering. It frames the rest of the survey of enjoyment, which goes on to describe food and sexual life across the realms.

There are two ways of consuming: consuming the objects of desire, and **consuming the true Dharma** (受用正法). The second differs in five ways: it is undefiled; it is final (it does not leave one wanting more); it is unwavering; it is not shared with other "wisdom-lives"; and it brings genuine pleasure that overcomes Māra.

On "not final", Master Cháng Bǎi quotes a Ming-dynasty song about greed, "Ten Discontents": get one thing, want the next, never satisfied. On Māra, both teachers say the most fundamental of the four Māras is the **Māra of affliction**. Master Cháng Bǎi: "The root of saṃsāra is affliction; without affliction all suffering ends."

subs.head: The body as a poisonous boil

blocks.text: "The bodies of beings in the three realms should be observed as a poisonous, feverish boil (毒熱癰), followed everywhere by its own underlying affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: the problem "is not in the heavens or under the earth; it is right here in one's own body".
Then each feeling is a symptom:

items: **painful feeling** is like the boil touched by something hot or caustic;
**pleasant feeling** is like the boil briefly touched by something cool. Master Cháng Bǎi: put ice on it and the pain eases for a moment, and it feels good, but the boil is still there;
**neutral feeling** is like the boil left untouched: still a boil.

blocks.text: The Buddha's words, quoted here: "Pleasant feeling is suffering through the **suffering of change**; painful feeling through the **suffering of pain**; neutral feeling through the **suffering of conditioned formations**." (Compare Day 7, where all existence was called the suffering of formations.)

Why single out neutral feeling for the suffering of formations, when all three involve it? Master Cháng Bǎi: "only in neutral feeling does the character of the suffering of formations appear distinctly." Venerable Miào Jìng adds that neutral feeling dulls us into not noticing anything is wrong.

The Buddha set the bliss of the attainment of cessation as foremost, but "this is the bliss of abiding, not the bliss of feeling". It is not something experienced by a conscious mind. Even the highest worldly "bliss" in this account is a matter of release, not of feeling.

Life in the three realms is sustained by three foods, **contact**, **mental intention**, and **consciousness**; edible food sustains only the desire realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first two belong to the sixth consciousness, consciousness-food to the ālayavijñāna (as on Day 13). Hell-beings have a subtle edible food, "a faintly stirring wind within their organs". Beings at the kalala stage and the desire-realm gods have a subtle food that leaves no waste. Master Cháng Bǎi adds a traditional detail: animals eat mostly in the afternoon, ghosts at night, humans three times a day, gods in the morning, Buddhas at midday, the origin of the monastic rule against eating after noon.

Hell-beings, in unbroken torment, have no sexual desire. Among humans and the lower gods, desire is satisfied by union. Higher up it grows lighter: the gods of the Time-Divisions need only embrace; Tuṣita gods only hold hands; those of Delighting in Transformation exchange a smile; the highest desire gods simply look at one another. The scale shows desire becoming subtler as merit grows, yet it is still desire; the form realm has none at all.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, in what five ways does consuming the true Dharma differ from consuming desire's objects?
options: undefiled, utterly final, one-pointedly certain, not shared with other wisdom-lives, and carrying genuine pleasure that overcomes Māra
quiz.why: "First, consuming the true Dharma is undefiled; second, it is utterly final; third, it is one-pointedly certain; fourth, it is not shared with other so-called wisdom-lives; fifth, it carries genuine pleasure, and overcomes the enemy that is Māra." §11–13 explain each. C lists ordinary wealth's faults.

quiz.q: The text says consuming the Dharma "overcomes the enemy that is Māra." Which of the four Māras do both teachers call the most fundamental?
options: the Māra of affliction — affliction is the root of saṃsāra
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The root of saṃsāra is affliction; without affliction all suffering ends — so affliction is the real Māra." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Really it is the inner Māra of affliction; that one is the most formidable." Master Cháng Bǎi also notes the *Pixunji* says this line "speaks only of the divine Māra," whose armies harass diligent meditators. So B is the literal referent; A is the teachers' point.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how should the body of beings in the three realms be observed?
options: as a poisonous, feverish boil, followed by its underlying affliction
quiz.why: "As a poisonous, feverish boil, followed everywhere by its own underlying affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: the problem "is not in the heavens or under the earth … it is right here in one's own body"; the underlying affliction has two layers — the seeds of affliction and the bodily result of afflicted karma. Master Cháng Bǎi cites the *Mohe Zhiguan*'s five impurities and its image of four snakes in a basket.

quiz.q: According to the Buddha's words quoted here, through which suffering is each feeling suffering?
quiz.why: "Pleasant feeling is suffering through the suffering of change; painful feeling is suffering through the suffering of pain itself; and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is suffering through the suffering inherent in all conditioned formations." Master Cháng Bǎi: the ever-flowing aggregates are never stable for an instant, so all three feelings carry the suffering of formations — it simply shows most clearly in neutral feeling.

quiz.q: All three feelings involve the suffering of formations. Why does the Buddha single out neutral feeling? How do the teachers explain it?
options: only in neutral feeling does the mark of formations show clearly — and neutral feeling dulls one into not noticing the problem
because it exists only in hell
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Only in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling does the character of the suffering of formations appear distinctly; that is why the Buddha says so." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only in neutral feeling does the mark of formations appear"; "neutral feeling makes one dull — one does not realise there is still a problem." He cites Master Yìnshùn's image of a man asleep in a ship heading for a reef.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which three foods sustain the lives of all beings in the three realms?
quiz.why: "It is by reason of three kinds of food — contact, mental intention, and consciousness — that all beings throughout the three realms have their lifespan sustained. The one remaining kind, edible food, sustains only the lifespan of beings within the desire realm." B fails because edible food belongs only to the desire realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm beings feed on meditative joy; formless beings have no body, so edible food does not arise.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how is the affliction of desire put to rest among the gods of Mastery over Others' Transformations?
quiz.why: The Four Great Kings and the Thirty-Three unite; the Time-Divisions gods "need only embrace"; Contentment, "only hold hands"; Delighting in Transformation, "exchange a smiling glance"; Mastery over Others' Transformations, "only look at one another." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The higher up, the thinner the desire." Desire-realm gods produce no impure fluid — only a breath of air.
